aboutMore: things i dont say out loud: i leave a little nice comment in the css of every layout i make. like /* if ur reading this hi. credit me. also ur doing great */. 9 out of 10 ppl never view source. dave did once. he said 'nice try dave' wasnt nice. it was. i also draw all my own pixel icons (16x16, ms paint zoomed 800%, 140 so far, my favorite is a 12 pixel heart). and i live in mesa where it was 112 on tuesday and the laptop is a space heater so i code w/ a wet washcloth on my neck. its fine. its a look.

blog.title: MONSOON SEASON: how i lost 4 hours of code and why i press ctrl+s 9 times a minute
blog.body: ok so in mesa we have monsoon season. its a month of the sky going purple at 4 pm and then the power doing a little flicker. i was 4 hours into a layout (kittyxcore's custom one, the checker one, 340 lines) and hadnt saved since the start bc i was 'in the zone.' the sky went purple. i said out loud 'dont.' it flickered. the screen went black. my fan stopped. the whole house went silent. for a second it was the quietest thing ive ever heard. then the power came back. notepad was gone. 4 hours. i sat on the floor. my dad walked in and said 'did it save.' i said no. he said 'ah.' and sat down on the floor next to me for a minute. then i rewrote the whole thing in 2 hrs 40 min bc i know it by heart now and that's the weird part: it was better. so i press ctrl+s 9 times a minute. i do it when im not coding. i just did it. ctrl+s.

blog.title: CLIENT TYPES: a field guide (no names) (all of the names)
blog.body: i've done layouts for 5 years so i can sort every client into 1 of 5 species. 1) THE PINK ONE: wants pink. then pinker. when u show her the pink she says 'its good but can it be more pink' and u say 'its pink on pink' and she says 'exactly.' (brittany) 2) THE DEADLINE ONE: sends 11 revisions, each with a due date. 'make the logo bigger' x4. 'smaller' x1. 'actually bigger.' (yvette, who is running for class president, so she is allowed) 3) THE MATRIX ONE: wants green rain on the loading screen. i said what loading screen. he said 'exactly.' (dave) 4) THE TILTED ONE: wants everything rotated 45 degrees. i did it. she said 'perfect.' my monitor now has a neck cramp. (paige) 5) THE ONE WHO SAYS 'SIMPLE': 6 hours. simple takes the longest. (josh) i love them all. i just want it noted that 'make it pop' is not a measurement.

blog.title: 16 x 16: a love letter to tiny things
blog.body: every icon i make is 16 pixels by 16 pixels. thats 256 squares. i do them in ms paint zoomed 800% and i click every square myself. i have 140. i dont use a program. the program makes them 'smooth' and i dont want smooth. i want the corners. a 16x16 heart has a whole personality (mine is 12 pixels, its my favorite, i dont know why 12 is better than 14 but it is). the secret is u get to decide what a face is made of. a smiley is 2 dots and a curve. thats 13 pixels. thats all u need to tell a person 'its ok.' i made a little envelope for my guestbook and 2 ppl told me it made them feel like mail. best review i've ever gotten. 256 squares. u can fit a whole mood in them. u can fit a pizza. i have a pizza.

blog.title: THE LITE LAYOUT PROJECT (what doug taught me)
blog.body: doug is on dial-up. so i made him a lite layout. first draft was 40k. he said that was '4 minutes.' i got it to 12k. he said '90 seconds.' i got it to 4k, then 2, then 1.4. it loads in 6 seconds. i have never worked so hard to make something look worse. no images. gray background. 4 lines of css. and it's the best thing i've made all year, which i did not expect. nothing to hide behind. i had to pick 1 color (#0000cc, doug's blue), 1 font (the one he already has) and a border that does all the heavy lifting. i said it was the ugliest thing i'd ever coded. i retract that. it wasn't ugly. it was honest. now i build every layout 'lite first': the doug version, then the fun on top, like a meal. doug once called my heavy layout dessert, so the lite one is dinner. i never thought of code as food. it works.
